title: The Reliability of the Bible: Prophecy and Fulfillment
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Nature of Biblical Prophecy
subpoints: Prophecy is the sovereign announcement of God's decrees, not mere forecasting.
God challenges idols to predict the future, a task only He can accomplish.
Biblical prophecy is specific and precise, unlike the ambiguous nature of pagan oracles.

outline.title: The Test of a True Prophet
subpoints: A prophet is validated if their predictions come to pass.
Biblical prophecies were exposed to falsification in their own time.
The Old Testament prophets were not rejected by their contemporaries, confirming their authenticity.

outline.title: Fulfillment in Christ
subpoints: The first promise in Genesis 3:15 is fulfilled in Jesus.
Specific details such as birthplace, entry into Jerusalem, and burial are precisely fulfilled.
The Gospels explicitly cite these events as fulfillments of Old Testament prophecy.

outline.title: Historical Evidence and the Dead Sea Scrolls
subpoints: Critics often claim prophecies were written after the fact due to their precision.
The discovery of the Dead Sea Scrolls, including the Great Isaiah Scroll, dates these texts centuries before Christ.
This archaeological evidence refutes the claim that Isaiah and Daniel were written post-event.

outline.title: Beyond Human Control
subpoints: Certain prophetic details, such as birthplace and tribal lineage, are beyond human manipulation.
The precision of these fulfillments points to a divine author behind the human writers.
The unity of Scripture demonstrates a single divine plan executed through history.

summary:
This lesson continues the series on the reliability of the Bible by examining the role of prophecy as a confirmation of Scripture's divine origin. The speaker emphasizes that biblical prophecy is not merely forecasting but the sovereign announcement of God's decrees, distinguishing it from the ambiguous and unfalsifiable nature of pagan oracles. By referencing Deuteronomy 18, the sermon highlights that Old Testament prophets were subject to immediate verification; their predictions were specific enough to be falsified if false, yet they were consistently fulfilled, validating their authority among their contemporaries.

A significant portion of the teaching focuses on the precise fulfillment of Messianic prophecies in the life of Jesus Christ. From the initial promise in Genesis 3:15 to specific details regarding His birth in Bethlehem, triumphal entry, and burial, the Gospels present these events as direct fulfillments of Old Testament texts. The sermon addresses common critical arguments that suggest these prophecies were written after the fact due to their accuracy. It counters this by citing the discovery of the Dead Sea Scrolls, particularly the Great Isaiah Scroll, which provides archaeological evidence that these texts existed centuries before the events they describe.

The lesson concludes by noting that many prophetic details, such as the Messiah's birthplace and tribal lineage, were beyond human control or manipulation. This precision and the overarching unity of the biblical narrative point to a single divine author guiding history, thereby confirming the Bible's reliability and internal consistency.
